editorial:
Imagine losing your whole family in a single night and having the science to bring them back. That's the wild setup of this sci-fi thriller. Keanu Reeves plays a brilliant researcher who works on transferring human minds into synthetic bodies. When a car crash kills his wife and kids, he breaks every rule to clone them and upload their memories. The movie has a tense, desperate vibe as he races against time and his own company. You feel his grief and panic in every scene.

The acting keeps you invested, especially Reeves carrying the emotional weight. The pacing moves fast once the cloning begins, though some plot holes might make you roll your eyes. The effects are decent but not flashy. If you enjoy mind-bending sci-fi with a human heart, this is worth a look. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final act, Reeves successfully clones his family and uploads their memories, but his company discovers what he did. A showdown reveals that the clones are actually perfect copies with no memory of dying. The twist is that the original family's consciousness was never truly saved, only duplicated. Reeves escapes with his cloned family to a new life, leaving behind the truth that the real versions are gone forever. The movie ends on a bittersweet note of a man living with copies of the people he lost.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sci-fi thrillers with emotional stakes and cloning themes.
